segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: easy English to help you learn. I'm Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. You can read along with this podcast and get a worksheet to help you learn

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hi Neil, how are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, Georgie. How are you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm also pretty good, thank you. Today we're talking about the ways we communicate.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Now, communicate, this means to speak or write to someone.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, we are communicating. Now, Georgie, we're speaking in person. That means we are both together to talk.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, do you like to speak to people in person?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, sometimes, yes. It depends, I guess. I like to speak to my friends in person, but I probably prefer to arrange things using email or something like that.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What about you? Do you like speaking on the phone?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No, I'm not a big fan of speaking on the phone. In fact, I almost hate speaking on the phone.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Really? What, to anybody?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No I speak to my family on the phone I speak to my friends on the phone as well but it has to be arranged in advance I don like it when people call me without telling me they going to call me But I think that a millennial thing

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What about you? Do you have the same problem?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I used to speak on the phone more, I guess.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's the strange thing about mobile phones. They do everything, but we don't really use them

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to talk on very much, do we?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No, no, we don't. I usually just like to communicate with people via

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: text. I find it, it's less distracting. When someone calls me, it takes my attention away from

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: the thing that I'm doing in that moment.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I know what you mean. Sometimes I think it's more

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: fun to have a conversation on an app because you can send emojis, you can send pictures,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and also you can drop and pick up the conversation over many hours.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, that's true. And also you can have group chats on apps as well. That's quite nice.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You can do group calls as well, but it's not as common. I don't do that much. Do you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, it's too much like work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you write letters anymore?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I don usually write letters but when it someone birthday or a special occasion I write cards and I like to write quite a lot like a meaningful message to my friends and family

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah It quite sad actually that people don write letters

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: much anymore because it's a different kind of communication. It's quite special. You spend a

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: lot of time writing the letter and maybe really thinking about what you want to say.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: yeah it takes more effort doesn't it yeah it's more more meaningful

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: are there any other ways

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: that you like to communicate with people do you do stuff on social media

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: yes in my old job i used

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: to have some social media accounts where i made um teaching content as well and i used to speak a

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: lot with people that i didn't know as well using their um instant messaging and comments as well

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't really like commenting on public posts. I feel it feels strange when a stranger says something about my point of view. Sometimes they're quite rude.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, it's a it's a difficult place to be the Internet. Neil, what's your favourite way to communicate?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think face communication with friends is the best because it the most fun the most immediate You get to see people faces You know how they responding or reacting So how about you Georgie

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think I like instant messaging apps because

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: they are the easiest way to communicate for me.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Let's recap some of the vocabulary we heard during the conversation. We had communicate,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: speak or write to someone.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We heard in person,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: meeting with someone

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: rather than talking on the phone

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or writing to them.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Prefer, like something more

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: than another thing.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, I prefer

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: instant messaging apps

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: to phoning someone.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we learnt some superlatives,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: ways to talk about something

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: being the best.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, we had best

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and we also heard easiest.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, for example,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think instant messaging

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: is the easiest way to talk to my friends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And that's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You can find a link in the notes for this episode.

segments.text: Next week, we'll talk about our wishes.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: See you then.
